html:
The Vallée de Mai is a palm forest on the island of Praslin in the Seychelles, home of the coco de mer, the palm with the largest seed in the world, found growing there by French explorers in 1768.

For centuries the huge double nuts had washed up on the shores of the Maldives and India, and sailors believed they grew on trees under the sea. Rulers prized them as cures and paid fortunes for them. Finding the trees on Praslin solved the mystery.

The forest was listed by UNESCO in 1983. It also shelters rare birds such as the black parrot. The nut is the emblem of the Seychelles and is carried home by tourists, under strict licence, one of the draws that the airport opened up.
